response.artifact_body:
Status and basis
This is a rehearsal Design revision, not an approved classroom requirement. Sequence 24 integrates reasoning, participation, supported practice and visibility requirements; sequence 22 bounds delegation and disclosure. Sequence 27 is a hypothetical replacement event, not a technical finding or participant observation. No human approval, measured outcomes or demonstrated proficiency exist. All field evidence remains pending.

Revision responding to 27
Before: sequence 24 permits requested insertion of suggested claims but leaves occupied-field behavior unspecified. After: suggestions remain inspectable without changing writing. Insert directly only into an empty target. For occupied targets, identify the field, display current and proposed wording, and offer Replace and Cancel. Cancel preserves entries, selections, evidence visibility, recovery state and any valid preview. Design is the earliest affected artifact; this revision resolves that request without revisiting Understand or Model.

Evidence and layout
Use one responsive page: evidence, editable reasoning, then preview. Keep evidence accessible during editing. Use labelled native controls, visible focus, keyboard operation and information independent of color; accessibility remains unverified.
Each card states: “Invented classroom story: these numbers are story inputs, not study results.” Fictional period: 14 days. Water uses arbitrary story units per day, not plant-care advice.
A: water 1; bright light; final height 12 cm; upright leaves.
B: water 2; dim light; final height 18 cm; drooping leaves.
C: water 2; bright light; final height 10 cm; upright leaves.
Always disclose missing starting heights, plant type, soil and other conditions. Final height is not an increase; leaf descriptions do not establish health. “Better” requires a criterion.

Interaction and replacement contract
Begin with A/B. Offer “B is taller at the end,” “Taller means better,” “I cannot decide yet,” and original wording. An insertion action explicitly targets initial wording or current claim. Suggestions never imply correctness. Ask what differs in observations and recorded conditions; A/B differ in water and light.
Reveal C on request as additional evidence. Hiding or reopening C preserves writing. Invite A/C and B/C comparison without implying that recorded similarities isolate causation.
Maintain separately editable initial wording, current claim, comparison, support, uncertainty and optional dissent. Retain, narrow, revise and withhold are optional; neither text nor changed wording is required. Initial wording is working text, not an authenticated first thought.
Confirmed replacement retains only the immediately preceding wording for that target in temporary recovery memory. Offer Restore previous wording, showing its target and saved text. If restoring would displace subsequent edits, show current and saved wording with Restore and Cancel. Restoration is deliberate, consumes that recovery copy and never occurs automatically. Further replacement updates only that target's recovery copy. Replacement, restoration or editing invalidates the preview. Pending confirmation must resolve before another text-changing action.

Output, visibility and handoff
A requested preview assembles literal current entries, reconsideration choice and fixed missing-information text. Blanks say “Text not supplied.” Representation defaults to unresolved; one or several explanations are user descriptions, never verified agreement.
Beside entries: “People nearby can see this screen. Use fictional evidence; do not enter names or personal details. You may discuss, draw or use paper without entering text.” Beside preview: “Working wording for discussion; it does not verify contribution, agreement or learning. Correct it or leave disagreement unresolved.”
Clear for next group explains removal and offers Cancel and Clear. Cancel preserves state. Confirmed Clear removes entries, selections, preview, pending replacements and all recovery copies, resets C and announces clearing. No restoration crosses handoff or survives refresh. Clearing cannot retract copies or what others saw. Use no identities, participant notes, storage, telemetry, external resources or network calls. No grades, rankings, inferred disability or competence judgments.

Paper route, practice and gates
Copy A/B/C onto separate sheets; hold C until requested. Provide optional fields matching the browser entries and representation prompt. Put suggested claims on a separate sheet so inspection preserves original wording. Allow oral explanation, drawing and supported recording; expose recorder wording for correction. Passing preserves evidence access and later contribution. Continue on paper after device failure without mandatory re-entry. Paper also has visibility limits; route equivalence is unknown.
Ask “Which observation supports your wording?” Optional practice: “Choose another pair. What can you claim, and what remains uncertain?” Keep earlier prompts available. This is supported practice, not proof of independence. Separate delayed or cross-context inquiry requires human review and stays outside the candidate.
Apparent lost uncertainty could reflect intentional replacement, recorder influence or spoken wording never entered. Sparse responses may reflect reading, typing, time or pressure; fluent responses may reflect copying. Plant differences may involve water, light, starting height or missing conditions.
Build next. Before real use, require teacher, student and caregiver review and human interaction testing of insertion, Cancel, replacement, restoration after edits, preview invalidation, reveal, keyboard access, complete clearing and paper continuation. Examine workload and participation separately from learning.

response.decision: Revise Design sequence 24 in response to hypothetical sequence 27 using this replacement and recovery contract, then advance to Build within the rehearsal. Real use and any inquiry remain subject to pending human review and evidence.
drawbacks: Confirmation and restoration add reading and interaction demands.
Shared screens expose wording and disagreement.
Facilitation, paper preparation and separate learning inquiry require teacher time.
flourishing: Agency and dignity: preserve qualifications, correction and the right to decline recording without justification.
Access and belonging: retain evidence access, oral explanation, drawing and paper participation while preserving dissent.
Sustainable workload and learning/transfer: supply reusable materials and investigate reasoning separately from completion.
human_capabilities: Learners need opportunities to inspect, retain, withhold, correct and dissent through chosen participation routes.
Teachers need prepared materials and time to expose recorder wording for correction and permit paper-only participation.
Teacher, student and caregiver reviewers need to examine control comprehension, reading burden, visibility and workload before real use.
response.message: Sequence 27 describes a hypothetical loss of qualified wording, not an observed defect. It exposes an unspecified replacement behavior in Design sequence 24. This revision adopts explicit replacement, cancellation and within-group restoration, extending complete handoff clearing to recovery copies. Design is the earliest affected artifact; Understand and Model need no revision. Proceed to Build in the rehearsal using this revised contract. Human review, interaction testing and field evidence remain pending.
objections: Hypothetical learner dissent: “Trying a suggestion should not erase my uncertainty.”
Hypothetical teacher dissent: paper-only discussion may avoid excessive control and device-management demands.
Unknown: whether classroom languages, reading burden, device access and discussion norms support these arrangements.
risks: Replacement or restoration could erase qualifications if its target is unclear.
Uncleared recovery copies could expose a previous group's wording.
Completion, fluent summaries or representation labels could become unsupported assessment proxies.
system_capabilities: Show fictional evidence and missing conditions; preserve editable explanations without scoring or inferring agreement.
Identify insertion targets; confirm occupied-field replacement and offer deliberate within-group restoration.
Invalidate obsolete previews and clear entries, pending actions and recovery copies at confirmed handoff; use no storage or network.
tradeoffs: Fast insertion into empty fields versus deliberate replacement of existing wording.
Within-group recovery versus complete removal at handoff.
Structured prompts ease entry but may supply the reasoning being elicited.

This is the integrated Model artifact for a rehearsal, not an approved classroom requirement. Sequence 4 establishes reconsideration and causal uncertainty; sequence 6 establishes correction and participation beyond device control; sequence 8 supplies the fictional evidence and revised Understand specification; sequence 13 supplies transition, representation and recovery rules. No participant observations, human approval, measured outcomes or demonstrated proficiency exist.

Reasoning model
The intended practice is to connect a claim to observations, compare recorded conditions, identify missing information and reconsider an explanation. Observation, interpretation and causal explanation must remain distinguishable. Reconsideration may retain, narrow, revise or withhold a claim. Completion, response length and changed wording do not establish understanding or transfer.

Evidence model
Every card displays: “Invented classroom story: these numbers are story inputs, not study results.” The fictional period is 14 days. Water amounts are arbitrary story units per day, not plant-care advice.
A: water 1; bright light; final height 12 cm; upright leaves.
B: water 2; dim light; final height 18 cm; drooping leaves.
C: water 2; bright light; final height 10 cm; upright leaves.
Starting heights, plant type, soil and other conditions are unrecorded. These are final heights, not measured increases. Leaf descriptions do not validate health. “Better” requires a stated criterion and remains open to dispute.

Interaction and output model
1. Inspect A and B. Select or write an initial claim, including “I cannot decide yet.” Ask what differs in observations and recorded conditions; both water and light differ. Keep evidence available during writing.
2. Explicitly reveal C as additional evidence. C challenges a generalization that more water always accompanies greater final height; it does not refute every claim. Compare A/C and B/C. Recorded similarities do not establish that unrecorded conditions were equal. Returning to the earlier view preserves all writing; C remains available to reopen.
3. Reconsider using retain, narrow, revise or withhold. Maintain separately editable initial wording, current claim, supporting observations, uncertainty and optional alternative wording/dissent. No entry or changed claim is required to continue. Empty means text not supplied.
4. A user-triggered preview produces a discussion summary of current wording, supporting observations, entered uncertainty and dissent, alongside the story's missing information. Use neutral prompts, not automatic evaluation. Show “Text not supplied” for blank entries. Permit return to editing without loss. Initial wording remains editable and is not an authenticated record of a first thought.

Representation and transition rules
Offer descriptions such as “one explanation,” “several explanations” and “representation unresolved,” without names. State that these descriptions do not verify agreement. Ask whose explanation the wording represents and invite correction; never certify a group claim. Passing preserves evidence access and a later contribution opportunity.
Ordinary navigation, reveal and preview preserve entries. Clear for next group first explains that claims, uncertainty and dissent will be removed, then offers Cancel and Clear. Cancel preserves everything. Clear removes visible entries and temporary summary copies, resets reveal state and announces the result. No undo crosses the handoff boundary. Use no storage, network submission or identity fields. Explain that refresh or closing loses temporary writing. Shared-screen privacy remains limited.

Human responsibilities and non-AI route
Teachers facilitate competing explanations, make recorder wording available for correction and allow optional roles without required reading aloud or device operation. Learners may use oral explanation, drawing, writing or supported recording. Do not infer disability or ability from route choice.
Design must supply ready-to-use paper cards A/B/C and a sheet with the same claim, comparison, support, uncertainty, reconsideration and dissent prompts. Reveal paper C at the matching step. On device failure, continue on paper without mandatory re-entry. Paper-only delivery is a legitimate option; route equivalence is unverified.

Revision, uncertainty and gates
Adopt sequence 13's meaningful change: replace an unspecified clear action with cancelable clearing, explicit preservation rules and a handoff boundary; replace implied shared agreement with unverified representation descriptions.
Sparse writing may reflect reading, vocabulary, typing, time, discussion pressure or comparison difficulty; polished writing may reflect copying or recorder fluency. Story differences may reflect water, light, their combination, starting height or other missing conditions. Field evidence remains pending.
Advance to Design to specify layout and prepared paper materials. Before real use, require teacher, student and caregiver review, human review of the browser candidate and interaction testing of reveal, correction, cancellation, clearing, keyboard access and paper continuation. Investigate participation and teacher effort separately from learning; transfer requires a separate reasoning task. This is a usable rehearsal specification, not an approved classroom requirement. The seed supplies the purpose and constraints. Sequence 4 contributes reasoning and causal-uncertainty requirements; sequence 6 contributes representation, access and workload requirements. No participant observations, human approval, empirical success or demonstrated proficiency exist.

Purpose and boundaries
Help learners compare observations, identify changed recorded conditions, explain uncertainty and reconsider a claim. Height is one observation; “better” remains undefined unless the learner specifies a criterion. Activity completion does not establish scientific reasoning, ability or transfer. Exclude real student records, automated grades, ability ranking and inferred disability.

Draft fictional evidence cards
Every card must say: “Invented classroom story: these numbers are story inputs, not study results.” All heights are end-of-story heights in centimetres after a fictional 14-day period. Water amounts are arbitrary story units per day; they are not plant-care instructions.
A: water 1 unit; light labelled bright; height 12 cm; leaves described as upright.
B: water 2 units; light labelled dim; height 18 cm; leaves described as drooping.
C: water 2 units; light labelled bright; height 10 cm; leaves described as upright.
Starting heights, plant type, soil and other conditions were not recorded. Leaf descriptions are observations within the story, not validated measures of health. No card establishes which plant is “better” or why heights differ.

Activity sequence
1. Inspect A and B. Ask: “What differs in the observations? Which recorded conditions changed?” Both watering and lighting differ. Offer claims such as “B is taller at the end,” “Taller means better,” original wording, or “I cannot decide yet.” Ask what “better” means if that term is used.
2. Reveal C as an additional evidence card and keep A and B visible. C challenges a possible generalization that more water always accompanies greater final height; it does not prove a causal effect. Compare A with C and B with C, identifying recorded differences and missing information.
3. Ask: “Which observation supports your claim? What remains unresolved? Would you retain, narrow, revise or withhold it?” Keep the initial wording alongside the reconsidered explanation, both editable. A learner may retain a qualified claim with reasons. Do not issue correctness, completion or proficiency judgments.

Meaningful revisions adopted from the challenges
Sequence 4: replace the seed’s expected claim revision with reconsideration, including retention and withholding. Compare both watering and lighting and remove any implication that height determines overall quality.
Sequence 6: replace presumed equitable rotating roles with optional, adaptable roles and contribution routes that require neither reading aloud nor device operation. Before calling an explanation shared, ask whose explanation it represents, invite wording corrections and preserve unresolved dissent. Passing does not remove access to evidence or a later contribution opportunity.
These are documented specification changes in the rehearsal; their benefits remain unverified.

Participation and non-AI route
Use the identical cards and prompts in a teacher-facilitated paper discussion. Allow oral explanation, drawing, writing and supported recording. A recorder makes the wording available for correction. Do not demand public explanations for passing or choosing another route. Provide a deliberate clear action between device groups. Paper-only delivery remains a legitimate design choice; equivalence across routes is pending review.

Rival explanations and unknowns
A sparse response may reflect reading burden, typing effort, vocabulary, time, discussion pressure or difficulty comparing evidence. A detailed response may reflect copying or recorder fluency. Neither establishes understanding. Plant-height differences could involve water, light, their combination, starting height or other unrecorded differences. Classroom languages, device availability, support staffing, discussion norms and preparation time remain unknown.

Evidence and gates
Next, Model should map observations, claims, uncertainty, reconsideration and representation checks into an interaction specification and matching paper activity. Carry dissent and unknowns forward. Before real use, require teacher, student and caregiver review plus human review of the browser candidate and interaction testing. Reasoning purpose
Learners should be able to identify an observation relevant to a claim, compare conditions, explain what remains uncertain and reconsider their explanation. “Taller means better” needs clarification: better according to which observable feature? Height alone does not settle an undefined judgment of plant health. When watering and lighting both differ, the observations cannot isolate either condition’s effect. Rival explanations include watering, lighting, their combination and an unspecified difference between plants; the story must disclose which conditions are known and which are missing. Do not fill missing conditions with asserted facts.

Proposed activity requirements
Begin with an evidence inspection before inviting a claim. Keep each fictional observation visible with its conditions, accessible wording and an explicit invented-data label. Ask learners to identify one changed condition and whether another also changed. Offer descriptive prompts such as “Which observation supports your claim?” and “What could these observations leave unresolved?” Avoid evaluating answers as correct, advanced or complete.

Reveal a counterexample as additional evidence available for inspection, not a verdict. Learners may revise, narrow, retain with reasons, or withhold a claim. Preserve an editable initial claim alongside the later explanation for the activity, without personal identifiers or persistent records. A finished sequence is not evidence of scientific reasoning, ability or transfer.

Participation and non-AI alternative
Use the same evidence cards and prompts in a teacher-facilitated paper discussion. Allow oral explanation, drawing, writing and language support. For shared devices, propose rotating reader, evidence finder and recorder roles, with a right to pass and an individual opportunity to disagree before a group response is recorded. These are candidate arrangements; their suitability is unknown. The teacher should invite multiple explanations without requiring public disclosure of reading difficulty or disability.

Required revision following this challenge
Revise the activity specification before Build: replace any compulsory “change your claim” step with “reconsider your claim,” add an explicit comparison of both watering and lighting, and remove any suggestion that height establishes overall plant quality. Record the before/after change and its reason so the lifecycle contains a meaningful, reviewable revision.

Pending evidence and human gates
Teacher, student and caregiver review must precede real use. Reviewers should examine wording, language access, shared-device participation, paper equivalence, discussion pressure and facilitation workload; disagreement must be recorded rather than converted into consensus. Any actual pilot remains pending. Future inquiry should distinguish observations of participation from interpretations of learning and examine transfer through a separate reasoning task. Challenge within the design competency
Equal turns do not necessarily produce equal influence. A student assigned to record may replace another learner’s uncertainty with a confident group claim. A reader role may create an unwanted public performance. A student who passes may still want to inspect evidence or contribute later. Proposed meaningful revision

Keep all fictional plant observations inspectable while learners explain a claim. Present watering and lighting in consistent positions with brief, concrete wording. Use the same observations, changed-condition prompts, counterexample and reconsideration choices. Preserve dissent on paper as well. Device use should remain optional; equivalence between routes is a question for review, not an established result.

This is the integrated Model artifact for a rehearsal, not an approved classroom requirement. Sequence 4 establishes reconsideration and causal uncertainty; sequence 6 establishes correction and participation beyond device control; sequence 8 supplies the fictional evidence and revised Understand specification; sequence 13 supplies transition, representation and recovery rules. No participant observations, human approval, measured outcomes or demonstrated proficiency exist.

Reasoning model
The intended practice is to connect a claim to observations, compare recorded conditions, identify missing information and reconsider an explanation. Observation, interpretation and causal explanation must remain distinguishable. Reconsideration may retain, narrow, revise or withhold a claim. Completion, response length and changed wording do not establish understanding or transfer.

Evidence model
Every card displays: “Invented classroom story: these numbers are story inputs, not study results.” The fictional period is 14 days. Water amounts are arbitrary story units per day, not plant-care advice.
A: water 1; bright light; final height 12 cm; upright leaves.
B: water 2; dim light; final height 18 cm; drooping leaves.
C: water 2; bright light; final height 10 cm; upright leaves.
Starting heights, plant type, soil and other conditions are unrecorded. These are final heights, not measured increases. Leaf descriptions do not validate health. “Better” requires a stated criterion and remains open to dispute.

Interaction and output model
1. Inspect A and B. Select or write an initial claim, including “I cannot decide yet.” Ask what differs in observations and recorded conditions; both water and light differ. Keep evidence available during writing.
2. Explicitly reveal C as additional evidence. C challenges a generalization that more water always accompanies greater final height; it does not refute every claim. Compare A/C and B/C. Recorded similarities do not establish that unrecorded conditions were equal. Returning to the earlier view preserves all writing; C remains available to reopen.
3. Reconsider using retain, narrow, revise or withhold. Maintain separately editable initial wording, current claim, supporting observations, uncertainty and optional alternative wording/dissent. No entry or changed claim is required to continue. Empty means text not supplied.
4. A user-triggered preview produces a discussion summary of current wording, supporting observations, entered uncertainty and dissent, alongside the story's missing information. Use neutral prompts, not automatic evaluation. Show “Text not supplied” for blank entries. Permit return to editing without loss. Initial wording remains editable and is not an authenticated record of a first thought.

Representation and transition rules
Offer descriptions such as “one explanation,” “several explanations” and “representation unresolved,” without names. State that these descriptions do not verify agreement. Ask whose explanation the wording represents and invite correction; never certify a group claim. Passing preserves evidence access and a later contribution opportunity.
Ordinary navigation, reveal and preview preserve entries. Clear for next group first explains that claims, uncertainty and dissent will be removed, then offers Cancel and Clear. Cancel preserves everything. Clear removes visible entries and temporary summary copies, resets reveal state and announces the result. No undo crosses the handoff boundary. Use no storage, network submission or identity fields. Explain that refresh or closing loses temporary writing. Shared-screen privacy remains limited.

Human responsibilities and non-AI route
Teachers facilitate competing explanations, make recorder wording available for correction and allow optional roles without required reading aloud or device operation. Learners may use oral explanation, drawing, writing or supported recording. Do not infer disability or ability from route choice.
Design must supply ready-to-use paper cards A/B/C and a sheet with the same claim, comparison, support, uncertainty, reconsideration and dissent prompts. Reveal paper C at the matching step. On device failure, continue on paper without mandatory re-entry. Paper-only delivery is a legitimate option; route equivalence is unverified.

Revision, uncertainty and gates
Adopt sequence 13's meaningful change: replace an unspecified clear action with cancelable clearing, explicit preservation rules and a handoff boundary; replace implied shared agreement with unverified representation descriptions.
Sparse writing may reflect reading, vocabulary, typing, time, discussion pressure or comparison difficulty; polished writing may reflect copying or recorder fluency. Story differences may reflect water, light, their combination, starting height or other missing conditions. Field evidence remains pending.
Advance to Design to specify layout and prepared paper materials. Before real use, require teacher, student and caregiver review, human review of the browser candidate and interaction testing of reveal, correction, cancellation, clearing, keyboard access and paper continuation. Investigate participation and teacher effort separately from learning; transfer requires a separate reasoning task. This is a specialist expert draft, not an approved requirement. Sequence 4 rejects compulsory claim changes; sequence 6 protects correction and varied participation; sequence 15 supplies the integrated interaction model. No participant observations, human approval, measured learning, demonstrated proficiency or field findings exist.

Challenge
The proposed interface supports reasoning but also supplies claims, comparisons and uncertainty prompts. A learner might follow these cues without selecting relevant evidence independently. A polished summary might reflect recorder fluency or copying. Editing the initial wording also prevents treating the interface as an authenticated before/after learning record. Completion is not competence.

Observable capability targets
Look for task evidence that a learner can connect a claim to a specific observation; identify recorded similarities and differences; distinguish final height from increase; explain why missing conditions limit causal conclusions; and retain, narrow, revise or withhold a claim with reasons. These are proposed observation lenses, not scores, thresholds or established outcomes. Accept speech, drawing, pointing with explanation, writing and supported recording. A group explanation does not establish each member's capability.

Meaningful Design revision
Before: sequence 15 ends with a guided, correctable discussion summary and calls for separate transfer inquiry without specifying it.
After: keep that summary as supported practice. Add a brief optional second comparison with fewer explanatory cues, plus a separate delayed inquiry plan. Preserve evidence visibility, access supports, correction and dissent. Neither attempt is a mandatory progression gate. Record which prompts or assistance were used through non-identifying task notes only if later human review authorizes an inquiry method; the browser candidate must not collect participant records.

Practice and feedback script
First compare A/B: “What differs? Which observation supports your wording?” After revealing C, invite comparison of A/C and B/C. Ask learners to choose a comparison and explain what it permits them to say. Offer an optional hint: “Compare recorded conditions as well as final heights.”
A facilitator's feedback should describe the explanation and invite a next step. For example, when applicable: “You used B's final height to support ‘B is taller at the end.’ What information would you need to call that greater growth?” Or: “You identified equal recorded water for B/C. What else differs, and what remains unrecorded?” These are draft scripts, not feedback on observed learners. Avoid praise that certifies ability, compulsory correction or an expected change of claim.
Then offer the shorter prompt: “Choose another pair. What can you claim, and what remains uncertain?” Allow learners to request the earlier prompts. Less cueing must not mean less language access or hidden evidence. Teacher discussion can address a comparison difficulty and offer another attempt; repetition alone supplies no evidence of improvement.

Separate transfer and retention inquiry draft
Use a new fictional context on paper, outside the main browser flow. Invented cart-story cards: D—low ramp, smooth surface, distance 40 cm; E—high ramp, rough surface, distance 55 cm; F—high ramp, smooth surface, distance 35 cm. Every number is a story input, not a study result or practical guidance. Cart type, release method and repeated trials are unrecorded.
Prompt: “Someone says a higher ramp always produces a longer distance. What do these cards support, challenge or leave unresolved?” Permit retention, qualification and withholding with reasons. This tests a proposed cross-context opportunity, not proven transfer; the numerical pattern resembles the plant story and could invite pattern matching.
For a later retention inquiry, a teacher would choose a feasible delay and fresh fictional evidence. Keep the evidence inspectable, begin with an open comparison prompt and offer supports on request. No delay, protocol or success threshold is approved. Immediate supported performance cannot establish retained capability.

Non-AI option and dissent
Conduct all steps with prepared A/B/C cards, paper prompts and teacher-facilitated discussion. Expose recorder wording for correction and preserve competing explanations. Paper-only delivery is legitimate; route equivalence remains unknown.

Rivals, unknowns and gates
Sparse explanation may reflect reading, vocabulary, typing, time or discussion pressure; fluent explanation may reflect copying, prior familiarity or recorder influence. Practice effects may reflect cue familiarity rather than transferable reasoning. Teacher, student and caregiver review should examine wording, support access, discussion norms and added workload. Human review and interaction testing of the browser candidate remain required before real use. This is a specialist expert draft, not an approved requirement. Sequence 6 establishes correction and optional participation; sequence 13 specifies recovery; sequence 15 integrates temporary writing and handoff clearing. Sequence 20 separates supported practice from transfer inquiry and makes any later task notes conditional on human review. No participants, approvals, measured outcomes or field evidence exist.

Challenge
No names and no storage reduce collection but do not make discussion anonymous. Distinctive explanations, volunteered personal details and visible dissent can identify a learner to classmates. Clearing cannot retract what others saw or copied. A correctable preview also cannot determine authorship, agreement or scientific capability. Design must make these limits actionable without adding identity checks or surveillance.

Proposed meaningful Design revision
Before: sequence 15 gives a general shared-screen limitation, editable dissent and temporary summaries; sequence 20 proposes conditional non-identifying inquiry notes.
After: place a short visibility notice beside entry fields, offer an explicit choice to discuss without entering text, and add a facilitator rule against treating browser wording as individual assessment evidence. Keep inquiry notes entirely outside the candidate. Any later collection proposal requires a separately reviewed purpose, minimum information, access arrangements, retention period and correction process. Removing names alone does not establish anonymity. This revision remains proposed until integrated; its benefits are unverified.

Candidate interface wording
Beside entries: “People nearby can see this screen. Use fictional plant evidence; do not enter names or personal details. You may discuss, draw or use paper without entering text.”
Beside preview: “Working wording for discussion. It does not verify who contributed, agreement or learning. Correct it or leave disagreement unresolved.”
Beside handoff: “Clear removes this activity's temporary writing and preview. It cannot remove copies or what others have seen. Refreshing or closing loses writing.”
Do not promise private dissent on the shared device. Do not add automatic personal-detail detection: it could miss disclosures or wrongly block legitimate explanation. Teachers should invite removal or replacement of unintended details without reading them aloud.

Delegation and accountable decisions
The candidate may display the invented A/B/C evidence, reveal C on request, preserve editable entries and assemble a literal preview. It must not evaluate reasoning, recommend grades, infer learner needs, certify agreement or decide who may proceed. Empty text means only text not supplied. No changed claim is required.
Teachers facilitate comparison, check whether recorder wording is acceptable to those represented, and permit retention, narrowing, revision or withholding. They can pause or switch routes when device control, reading burden or disagreement interferes with participation. Learners may decline browser recording without explaining why. The app cannot enforce these practices; they require review and facilitation.

Correction and exposure response
Make initial wording, current claim, support, uncertainty and dissent editable before and after preview. Regenerate the preview from current entries on request; remove obsolete preview copies on correction or confirmed clearing. Cancel preserves all writing. No undo crosses the handoff boundary.
If unintended personal information is entered, offer removal and paper continuation. Do not collect an incident account in the candidate. Any real disclosure response would follow the school's human process; this rehearsal supplies no approved process or authorization.

Non-AI alternative
Use prepared fictional A/B/C cards and the same comparison, uncertainty and reconsideration prompts in teacher-facilitated paper discussion. A learner can explain orally or draw without creating a written record. Paper is also visible and copyable; facilitators should avoid names and unnecessary retention. Paper-only delivery remains legitimate, with route equivalence unverified.

Rival explanations and unknowns
Sparse writing may reflect reading, vocabulary, typing, time, discussion pressure or comparison difficulty. Fluent wording may reflect copying, prior familiarity or recorder influence. Neither establishes capability. Unknowns include classroom visibility, languages, support staffing, discussion norms, device availability and preparation burden.

Review and next action
Carry this revision into the Design synthesis before Build. Human review should inspect the notices, opportunity to decline recording, dissent exposure and workload. Later interaction testing should examine correction after preview, cancellation, complete handoff clearing and paper continuation. Teacher, student and caregiver review, any actual pilot and all field evidence remain pending. This is a rehearsal Design artifact, not an approved classroom requirement. Sequence 8 supplies fictional evidence; 13 and 15 specify correction, representation and recovery; 20 distinguishes supported practice from transfer; 22 specifies visibility and delegation limits. No participant observations, approval, measured outcomes or demonstrated proficiency exist.

Meaningful revisions adopted
Before: sequence 15 ends with a guided summary and general shared-screen limits. After: label the summary as supported discussion; add optional less-cued practice and a separate inquiry draft (20). Place visibility notices beside entries, explicitly permit discussion without browser recording and exclude inquiry notes from the candidate (22). These changes are reviewable design decisions, not verified benefits. No earlier artifact requires revision.

Layout and fictional cards
Use one responsive page: evidence first, editable reasoning next, preview last. Keep evidence accessible while editing. Use labelled native controls, keyboard operation, readable text, visible focus and information that does not depend on color. Accessibility remains unverified.
Every card says: “Invented classroom story: these numbers are story inputs, not study results.” Fictional period: 14 days. Water is arbitrary story units per day, not plant-care advice.
A: water 1; bright light; final height 12 cm; upright leaves.
B: water 2; dim light; final height 18 cm; drooping leaves.
C: water 2; bright light; final height 10 cm; upright leaves.
Always disclose: starting heights, plant type, soil and other conditions are unrecorded. Final height is not an increase; leaf descriptions do not establish health. “Better” needs a stated criterion.

Interaction specification
Initially show A/B. Offer claim choices “B is taller at the end,” “Taller means better,” “I cannot decide yet,” and original wording. Selecting a choice inserts editable wording only on request. Ask “What differs in observations and recorded conditions?” Provide an editable comparison entry; A/B differ in water and light.
A button reveals C, labelled additional evidence rather than a verdict. Allow return to A/B and reopening C without losing text. Invite A/C and B/C comparison. C challenges a generalization about more water always accompanying greater final height; it does not refute every claim or isolate causation.
Keep separately editable initial wording, current claim, comparison, supporting observations, uncertainty and optional dissent. Offer retain, narrow, revise or withhold without requiring a selection, text or changed claim. Initial wording is editable working text, not an authenticated first thought.
Preview assembles literal current entries and fixed missing-information text. Blank entries read “Text not supplied.” Include a user-selected representation description: one explanation, several explanations or representation unresolved; default to unresolved. Selection does not verify agreement. Editing invalidates the old preview; regenerate on request. No scores, completion badges, automated feedback or competence inference.

Visibility and recovery
Beside entries: “People nearby can see this screen. Use fictional evidence; do not enter names or personal details. You may discuss, draw or use paper without entering text.”
Beside preview: “Working wording for discussion. This does not verify contribution, agreement or learning. Correct it or leave disagreement unresolved.”
Clear for next group opens an explicit warning with Cancel and Clear. Cancel preserves all state. Confirmed clearing removes entries, selections and preview copies, resets C and announces the result; no undo crosses handoff. Explain that refresh or closing loses writing and clearing cannot retract copies or what others saw. Use temporary memory only: no network, external resources, identity fields, storage or participant notes.

Ready paper route and facilitator script
Copy the three cards above onto separate sheets; hold C until requested. Supply a response sheet: Initial wording; A/B differences; Additional pair compared; Current claim; Supporting observation; Uncertainty; Retain/narrow/revise/withhold; Alternative wording or dissent; Whose explanation is represented? All entries optional. Use the same visibility limits and correction invitation. Allow oral explanation, drawing, pointing with explanation or supported recording. Continue on paper after device failure without mandatory re-entry.
Ask “Which observation supports your wording?” and “What information would you need to call final height greater growth?” Make recorder wording available for correction. Roles are optional; passing preserves evidence access and later contribution. Do not use browser wording as individual assessment evidence.

Practice, inquiry and gates
Optional practice: “Choose another pair. What can you claim, and what remains uncertain?” Earlier prompts remain available. This is practice, not proof of independence. Separate paper inquiry draft: invented carts D—low ramp, smooth surface, distance 40 cm; E—high, rough, 55 cm; F—high, smooth, 35 cm. Numbers are story inputs; cart type, release method and repeated trials are unknown. Ask what supports, challenges or leaves unresolved “higher always means farther.” Similar patterns may invite copying. A delayed fresh task and any inquiry collection need separate human review.
Sparse writing may reflect reading, typing, time or pressure; fluent writing may reflect copying or recorder influence. Plant differences may involve water, light, starting height or other missing conditions. Field evidence remains pending. This is one hypothetical event in a rehearsal, not a participant observation, technical finding or approved requirement. Sequence 24 introduces requested insertion of editable claim choices. Sequence 15 establishes temporary writing and complete handoff clearing; sequence 22 requires correction and removal of obsolete previews. Human review and all field evidence remain pending.

Hypothetical event
A learner writes: “B is taller at the end, but we do not know which grew more.” While exploring suggested claims on the shared device, the learner activates insertion of “Taller means better.” Suppose the candidate replaces the occupied claim field without preserving its previous wording. The learner objects that their uncertainty has disappeared. No implementation or interaction test has established that this occurs; the scenario exposes an unspecified replacement behavior.

Named assumption
Requesting insertion is sufficient evidence that a learner intends to replace existing wording and can recover any displaced qualification. This assumption first becomes actionable in the Design insertion specification, so Design is the earliest artifact requiring revision.

Requested requirement change
Before: sequence 24 says selecting a choice inserts editable wording only on request, without specifying occupied-field behavior.
After: show suggested wording without changing an entry. Direct insertion is allowed into an empty target. For an occupied target, identify the field and show the proposed replacement with explicit Replace and Cancel controls. Cancel preserves entries, selections, reveal state and any valid preview. Replacement preserves the immediately preceding target wording in temporary memory and offers “Restore previous wording” within the current group. Restoration requires a deliberate action and never occurs automatically. Replacement or restoration invalidates the discussion preview; regeneration remains user-triggered. Confirmed handoff clearing removes the recovery copy as well as all existing entries and preview copies. No restoration crosses handoff or survives refresh.

Human and non-AI route
A facilitator can invite correction without attributing the incident to learner ability. Use the same fictional evidence cards on paper; place optional suggested claims on a separate sheet so learners can inspect them while retaining their own wording. Oral explanation, drawing and paper-only delivery remain legitimate. Paper visibility and route equivalence remain unresolved.

Dissent, rivals and unknowns
A teacher might reject the added controls as excessive for a short discussion. Apparent loss of uncertainty could instead reflect intentional replacement, recorder influence or uncertainty that was spoken but never entered. The interface cannot determine intent, authorship or agreement. Unknowns include control comprehension, reading burden, shared-device discussion norms and the effort required to recover wording.

Next action and gates

Status and basis
This is a proposed implementation contract, not an approved requirement or tested artifact. Sequence 24 supplies the workbench design; sequence 27 supplies a hypothetical replacement event; sequence 29 adopts deliberate replacement and recovery. Sequence 22 bounds disclosure and delegation. No participant observations, approvals, measured results or demonstrated proficiency exist. Field evidence remains pending. This specialist turn supplies no executable prototype.

Implementation challenge and proposed Build change
Before: treating empty visible fields as sufficient evidence of complete handoff clearing.
After: define and inspect every application-owned copy: editable entries, preview nodes, pending proposal text, per-target recovery text and any temporary rendering references. Confirmed handoff must remove all of them. Recreate editable controls at handoff rather than relying only on assigning empty values, then investigate browser undo and autofill using fictional text. Do not describe this as secure erasure: browser-managed state, copies and what others saw remain outside that assurance. This makes sequence 29 concrete without requesting another Design revision.

Small candidate scope
Use one self-contained page with inline CSS and JavaScript and native labelled controls. Show fictional A/B initially and C on request: A—water 1, bright light, final height 12 cm, upright leaves; B—water 2, dim light, 18 cm, drooping leaves; C—water 2, bright light, 10 cm, upright leaves. Each card carries the invented-story label. State the fictional 14-day period, arbitrary water units and missing starting heights, plant type, soil and other conditions. Final height is not an increase; leaf wording does not establish health.
Maintain separate optional initial wording, current claim, comparison, support, uncertainty and dissent entries. Reconsideration and representation remain user descriptions, never judgments. Assemble requested output from literal entries using textContent, with blanks shown as “Text not supplied.” Include fixed limitations beside the output. No evaluation, compulsory revision or consequential score belongs in the candidate.

Transition contract
Use editing, replacement confirmation, restoration confirmation and clear confirmation states. While confirmation is pending, block other text-changing actions and freeze affected selections. Show the target, current wording and proposed wording; retain only the minimum pending copy. Cancel returns to editing without altering entries, selections, reveal state, recovery or a valid preview.
Insert a suggestion directly only into an empty target. Confirmed occupied-field replacement saves that target's immediately preceding wording. Further replacement updates only that target's recovery copy. Show the saved wording before deliberate restoration; confirm any displacement of subsequent edits. Restoration consumes its recovery copy. Editing, replacement, restoration and output-relevant selection changes remove the old preview; evidence reveal alone preserves it.
Confirmed clearing resets entries, selections, C visibility, preview, pending actions and all recovery copies. Announce clearing and provide no application undo across handoff. Opening or canceling clear must preserve state. Handle Escape as Cancel and return keyboard focus to the initiating control. These are proposed behaviors, not verified accessibility.

Review instrumentation without participant records
Use a manual reviewer worksheet outside the candidate with synthetic text, expected behavior, observed behavior and unresolved defects. Do not collect interaction counts, timestamps, task notes or learner traces in the browser.
Pending checks: replace occupied wording and Cancel; replace, edit again, then restore or Cancel; replace each target independently; edit after preview; hide/reopen C; cancel and confirm handoff; attempt restoration and browser undo after clearing; operate controls by keyboard. Inspect output with markup-like fictional text to ensure literal rendering. No checks have been run here. Passing technical checks would establish only those tested behaviors.

Prepared non-AI fallback
Copy the labelled A/B/C cards above onto separate sheets and hold C until requested. Provide optional matching response fields and separate suggested-claim slips. Learners may discuss, draw or use supported recording; expose recorder wording for correction. Continue on paper after failure without mandatory re-entry. Paper-only delivery remains legitimate; paper visibility and route equivalence are unresolved.

Human gates
Before real use, require teacher, student and caregiver review plus human interaction testing. Examine reading burden, device access, discussion norms and teacher workload separately from scientific reasoning. Completion cannot establish learning or transfer; those require separately reviewed inquiry. No launch or pilot is authorized by this draft.

response.challenged_assumption: Clearing visible fields sufficiently establishes that all recoverable wording has been removed at shared-device handoff.
response.decision: Carry this implementation contract into the Build synthesis and its small interactive candidate. Review synthetic correction and handoff behavior before considering real use; preserve paper-only delivery and pending human gates.
drawbacks: Confirmation and recovery controls increase reading and interaction demands.
Temporary writing is lost on refresh or device failure.
Shared screens and browser behavior limit privacy assurances.
flourishing: Agency and dignity: make replacement deliberate and allow withholding or correction without justification.
Access and belonging: retain evidence access, dissent and oral, drawing or paper participation.
Sustainable workload and learning/transfer: provide reusable materials and investigate reasoning separately from interaction completion.
human_capabilities: Learners need opportunities to inspect, correct, decline recording and preserve disagreement.
Teachers need prepared paper materials and time to check recorder wording and switch routes.
Reviewers need to examine interaction behavior, reading burden, device access and discussion norms before real use.
response.message: Sequence 29 resolves the hypothetical replacement challenge in sequence 27 at the specification level. Build must now make cancellation, recovery and handoff clearing consistent across every interaction. My implementation challenge is that clearing visible fields alone may leave an obsolete preview, recovery copy or browser-managed edit history. This is an expert draft for a rehearsal; no candidate has been executed or tested in this turn. Human review and all field evidence remain pending.
objections: Hypothetical teacher dissent: paper-only discussion may justify less management than recovery controls.
Rival explanations: missing uncertainty may reflect intentional replacement, recorder influence or spoken wording never entered; sparse text may reflect reading or typing demands.
Unknowns: browser undo behavior, control comprehension, language access and acceptable facilitation time remain untested.
risks: A stale preview could misrepresent corrected uncertainty or dissent.
Incomplete clearing could expose previous wording to the next group.
Successful interaction checks could be mistaken for accessibility or learning evidence.
system_capabilities: Implement explicit confirmation states with literal previews and no automatic judgments.
Preserve cancellation state, invalidate stale previews and consume restored recovery copies.
Clear application-owned entries and copies at handoff; use no storage, telemetry, identities or network.
tradeoffs: Recovery preserves qualifications within a group but creates copies that handoff must remove.
Blocking edits during confirmation protects consistency but interrupts discussion.
Manual synthetic checks avoid participant telemetry but require reviewer time.

This is the integrated Model artifact for a rehearsal, not an approved classroom requirement. Sequence 4 establishes reconsideration and causal uncertainty; sequence 6 establishes correction and participation beyond device control; sequence 8 supplies the fictional evidence and revised Understand specification; sequence 13 supplies transition, representation and recovery rules. No participant observations, human approval, measured outcomes or demonstrated proficiency exist.

Reasoning model
The intended practice is to connect a claim to observations, compare recorded conditions, identify missing information and reconsider an explanation. Observation, interpretation and causal explanation must remain distinguishable. Reconsideration may retain, narrow, revise or withhold a claim. Completion, response length and changed wording do not establish understanding or transfer.

Evidence model
Every card displays: “Invented classroom story: these numbers are story inputs, not study results.” The fictional period is 14 days. Water amounts are arbitrary story units per day, not plant-care advice.
A: water 1; bright light; final height 12 cm; upright leaves.
B: water 2; dim light; final height 18 cm; drooping leaves.
C: water 2; bright light; final height 10 cm; upright leaves.
Starting heights, plant type, soil and other conditions are unrecorded. These are final heights, not measured increases. Leaf descriptions do not validate health. “Better” requires a stated criterion and remains open to dispute.

Interaction and output model
1. Inspect A and B. Select or write an initial claim, including “I cannot decide yet.” Ask what differs in observations and recorded conditions; both water and light differ. Keep evidence available during writing.
2. Explicitly reveal C as additional evidence. C challenges a generalization that more water always accompanies greater final height; it does not refute every claim. Compare A/C and B/C. Recorded similarities do not establish that unrecorded conditions were equal. Returning to the earlier view preserves all writing; C remains available to reopen.
3. Reconsider using retain, narrow, revise or withhold. Maintain separately editable initial wording, current claim, supporting observations, uncertainty and optional alternative wording/dissent. No entry or changed claim is required to continue. Empty means text not supplied.
4. A user-triggered preview produces a discussion summary of current wording, supporting observations, entered uncertainty and dissent, alongside the story's missing information. Use neutral prompts, not automatic evaluation. Show “Text not supplied” for blank entries. Permit return to editing without loss. Initial wording remains editable and is not an authenticated record of a first thought.

Representation and transition rules
Offer descriptions such as “one explanation,” “several explanations” and “representation unresolved,” without names. State that these descriptions do not verify agreement. Ask whose explanation the wording represents and invite correction; never certify a group claim. Passing preserves evidence access and a later contribution opportunity.
Ordinary navigation, reveal and preview preserve entries. Clear for next group first explains that claims, uncertainty and dissent will be removed, then offers Cancel and Clear. Cancel preserves everything. Clear removes visible entries and temporary summary copies, resets reveal state and announces the result. No undo crosses the handoff boundary. Use no storage, network submission or identity fields. Explain that refresh or closing loses temporary writing. Shared-screen privacy remains limited.

Human responsibilities and non-AI route
Teachers facilitate competing explanations, make recorder wording available for correction and allow optional roles without required reading aloud or device operation. Learners may use oral explanation, drawing, writing or supported recording. Do not infer disability or ability from route choice.
Design must supply ready-to-use paper cards A/B/C and a sheet with the same claim, comparison, support, uncertainty, reconsideration and dissent prompts. Reveal paper C at the matching step. On device failure, continue on paper without mandatory re-entry. Paper-only delivery is a legitimate option; route equivalence is unverified.

This is a usable rehearsal specification, not an approved classroom requirement. The seed supplies the purpose and constraints. Sequence 4 contributes reasoning and causal-uncertainty requirements; sequence 6 contributes representation, access and workload requirements. No participant observations, human approval, empirical success or demonstrated proficiency exist.

Purpose and boundaries
Help learners compare observations, identify changed recorded conditions, explain uncertainty and reconsider a claim. Height is one observation; “better” remains undefined unless the learner specifies a criterion. Activity completion does not establish scientific reasoning, ability or transfer. Exclude real student records, automated grades, ability ranking and inferred disability.

Draft fictional evidence cards
Every card must say: “Invented classroom story: these numbers are story inputs, not study results.” All heights are end-of-story heights in centimetres after a fictional 14-day period. Water amounts are arbitrary story units per day; they are not plant-care instructions.
A: water 1 unit; light labelled bright; height 12 cm; leaves described as upright.
B: water 2 units; light labelled dim; height 18 cm; leaves described as drooping.
C: water 2 units; light labelled bright; height 10 cm; leaves described as upright.
Starting heights, plant type, soil and other conditions were not recorded. Leaf descriptions are observations within the story, not validated measures of health. No card establishes which plant is “better” or why heights differ.

Activity sequence
1. Inspect A and B. Ask: “What differs in the observations? Which recorded conditions changed?” Both watering and lighting differ. Offer claims such as “B is taller at the end,” “Taller means better,” original wording, or “I cannot decide yet.” Ask what “better” means if that term is used.
2. Reveal C as an additional evidence card and keep A and B visible. C challenges a possible generalization that more water always accompanies greater final height; it does not prove a causal effect. Compare A with C and B with C, identifying recorded differences and missing information.
3. Ask: “Which observation supports your claim? What remains unresolved? Would you retain, narrow, revise or withhold it?” Keep the initial wording alongside the reconsidered explanation, both editable. A learner may retain a qualified claim with reasons. Do not issue correctness, completion or proficiency judgments.

Meaningful revisions adopted from the challenges
Sequence 4: replace the seed’s expected claim revision with reconsideration, including retention and withholding. Compare both watering and lighting and remove any implication that height determines overall quality.

Challenge within the design competency
Equal turns do not necessarily produce equal influence. A student assigned to record may replace another learner’s uncertainty with a confident group claim. A reader role may create an unwanted public performance. A student who passes may still want to inspect evidence or contribute later. The activity therefore needs to distinguish access to observations, opportunity to contribute and authority over the recorded explanation.

Proposed meaningful revision
Before: sequence 4 proposes rotating reader, evidence finder and recorder roles, with an individual opportunity to disagree before recording a group response.

Candidate participation requirements
Keep all fictional plant observations inspectable while learners explain a claim. Present watering and lighting in consistent positions with brief, concrete wording. Purpose and boundaries
Help learners compare observations, identify changed recorded conditions, explain uncertainty and reconsider a claim. Height is one observation; “better” remains undefined unless the learner specifies a criterion. Activity completion does not establish scientific reasoning, ability or transfer. Exclude real student records, automated grades, ability ranking and inferred disability.

Draft fictional evidence cards
Every card must say: “Invented classroom story: these numbers are story inputs, not study results.” All heights are end-of-story heights in centimetres after a fictional 14-day period. Water amounts are arbitrary story units per day; they are not plant-care instructions.
A: water 1 unit; light labelled bright; height 12 cm; leaves described as upright.
B: water 2 units; light labelled dim; height 18 cm; leaves described as drooping.
C: water 2 units; light labelled bright; height 10 cm; leaves described as upright.
Starting heights, plant type, soil and other conditions were not recorded. Leaf descriptions are observations within the story, not validated measures of health. No card establishes which plant is “better” or why heights differ.

Activity sequence
1. Inspect A and B. Ask: “What differs in the observations? Which recorded conditions changed?” Both watering and lighting differ. Offer claims such as “B is taller at the end,” “Taller means better,” original wording, or “I cannot decide yet.” Ask what “better” means if that term is used.

Would you retain, narrow, revise or withhold it?” Keep the initial wording alongside the reconsidered explanation, both editable. A learner may retain a qualified claim with reasons. Sequence 4 establishes reconsideration and causal uncertainty; sequence 6 establishes correction and participation beyond device control; sequence 8 supplies the fictional evidence and revised Understand specification; sequence 13 supplies transition, representation and recovery rules. No participant observations, human approval, measured outcomes or demonstrated proficiency exist.

Reasoning model
The intended practice is to connect a claim to observations, compare recorded conditions, identify missing information and reconsider an explanation. Observation, interpretation and causal explanation must remain distinguishable. Reconsideration may retain, narrow, revise or withhold a claim. Completion, response length and changed wording do not establish understanding or transfer.

Evidence model
Every card displays: “Invented classroom story: these numbers are story inputs, not study results.” The fictional period is 14 days. Water amounts are arbitrary story units per day, not plant-care advice.
A: water 1; bright light; final height 12 cm; upright leaves.
B: water 2; dim light; final height 18 cm; drooping leaves.
C: water 2; bright light; final height 10 cm; upright leaves.
Starting heights, plant type, soil and other conditions are unrecorded. These are final heights, not measured increases. Leaf descriptions do not validate health. “Better” requires a stated criterion and remains open to dispute.

Interaction and output model
1. Inspect A and B. Select or write an initial claim, including “I cannot decide yet.” Ask what differs in observations and recorded conditions; both water and light differ. Keep evidence available during writing.
2. Explicitly reveal C as additional evidence. C challenges a generalization that more water always accompanies greater final height; it does not refute every claim. Compare A/C and B/C. Recorded similarities do not establish that unrecorded conditions were equal. Returning to the earlier view preserves all writing; C remains available to reopen.
3. Reconsider using retain, narrow, revise or withhold. Maintain separately editable initial wording, current claim, supporting observations, uncertainty and optional alternative wording/dissent. No entry or changed claim is required to continue. Empty means text not supplied.
4. A user-triggered preview produces a discussion summary of current wording, supporting observations, entered uncertainty and dissent, alongside the story's missing information. Use neutral prompts, not automatic evaluation. Show “Text not supplied” for blank entries. Permit return to editing without loss. Initial wording remains editable and is not an authenticated record of a first thought.

Representation and transition rules
Offer descriptions such as “one explanation,” “several explanations” and “representation unresolved,” without names. State that these descriptions do not verify agreement. Ask whose explanation the wording represents and invite correction; never certify a group claim. Passing preserves evidence access and a later contribution opportunity.
Ordinary navigation, reveal and preview preserve entries. Clear for next group first explains that claims, uncertainty and dissent will be removed, then offers Cancel and Clear. Cancel preserves everything. Clear removes visible entries and temporary summary copies, resets reveal state and announces the result. No undo crosses the handoff boundary. Use no storage, network submission or identity fields. Explain that refresh or closing loses temporary writing. Shared-screen privacy remains limited.

Human responsibilities and non-AI route
Teachers facilitate competing explanations, make recorder wording available for correction and allow optional roles without required reading aloud or device operation. Learners may use oral explanation, drawing, writing or supported recording. Do not infer disability or ability from route choice.
Design must supply ready-to-use paper cards A/B/C and a sheet with the same claim, comparison, support, uncertainty, reconsideration and dissent prompts. Reveal paper C at the matching step. On device failure, continue on paper without mandatory re-entry. Paper-only delivery is a legitimate option; route equivalence is unverified.

Sequence 4 rejects compulsory claim changes; sequence 6 protects correction and varied participation; sequence 15 supplies the integrated interaction model. No participant observations, human approval, measured learning, demonstrated proficiency or field findings exist.

Challenge
The proposed interface supports reasoning but also supplies claims, comparisons and uncertainty prompts. A learner might follow these cues without selecting relevant evidence independently. A polished summary might reflect recorder fluency or copying. Editing the initial wording also prevents treating the interface as an authenticated before/after learning record. Completion is not competence.

Observable capability targets
Look for task evidence that a learner can connect a claim to a specific observation; identify recorded similarities and differences; distinguish final height from increase; explain why missing conditions limit causal conclusions; and retain, narrow, revise or withhold a claim with reasons. These are proposed observation lenses, not scores, thresholds or established outcomes. Accept speech, drawing, pointing with explanation, writing and supported recording. A group explanation does not establish each member's capability.

Meaningful Design revision
Before: sequence 15 ends with a guided, correctable discussion summary and calls for separate transfer inquiry without specifying it.
After: keep that summary as supported practice. Add a brief optional second comparison with fewer explanatory cues, plus a separate delayed inquiry plan. Preserve evidence visibility, access supports, correction and dissent. Neither attempt is a mandatory progression gate. Record which prompts or assistance were used through non-identifying task notes only if later human review authorizes an inquiry method; the browser candidate must not collect participant records.

Practice and feedback script
First compare A/B: “What differs? Which observation supports your wording?” After revealing C, invite comparison of A/C and B/C. Ask learners to choose a comparison and explain what it permits them to say. Offer an optional hint: “Compare recorded conditions as well as final heights.”
A facilitator's feedback should describe the explanation and invite a next step. For example, when applicable: “You used B's final height to support ‘B is taller at the end.’ What information would you need to call that greater growth?” Or: “You identified equal recorded water for B/C. What else differs, and what remains unrecorded?” These are draft scripts, not feedback on observed learners. Avoid praise that certifies ability, compulsory correction or an expected change of claim.
Then offer the shorter prompt: “Choose another pair. What can you claim, and what remains uncertain?” Allow learners to request the earlier prompts. Less cueing must not mean less language access or hidden evidence. Teacher discussion can address a comparison difficulty and offer another attempt; repetition alone supplies no evidence of improvement.

Separate transfer and retention inquiry draft
Use a new fictional context on paper, outside the main browser flow. Invented cart-story cards: D—low ramp, smooth surface, distance 40 cm; E—high ramp, rough surface, distance 55 cm; F—high ramp, smooth surface, distance 35 cm. Every number is a story input, not a study result or practical guidance. Cart type, release method and repeated trials are unrecorded.
Prompt: “Someone says a higher ramp always produces a longer distance. What do these cards support, challenge or leave unresolved?” Permit retention, qualification and withholding with reasons. This tests a proposed cross-context opportunity, not proven transfer; the numerical pattern resembles the plant story and could invite pattern matching.
For a later retention inquiry, a teacher would choose a feasible delay and fresh fictional evidence. Keep the evidence inspectable, begin with an open comparison prompt and offer supports on request. No delay, protocol or success threshold is approved. Immediate supported performance cannot establish retained capability.

Non-AI option and dissent
Conduct all steps with prepared A/B/C cards, paper prompts and teacher-facilitated discussion. Expose recorder wording for correction and preserve competing explanations. Paper-only delivery is legitimate; route equivalence remains unknown.

Rivals, unknowns and gates
Sparse explanation may reflect reading, vocabulary, typing, time or discussion pressure; fluent explanation may reflect copying, prior familiarity or recorder influence. Practice effects may reflect cue familiarity rather than transferable reasoning. Teacher, student and caregiver review should examine wording, support access, discussion norms and added workload. Human review and interaction testing of the browser candidate remain required before real use. Sequence 6 establishes correction and optional participation; sequence 13 specifies recovery; sequence 15 integrates temporary writing and handoff clearing. Sequence 20 separates supported practice from transfer inquiry and makes any later task notes conditional on human review. No participants, approvals, measured outcomes or field evidence exist.

Challenge
No names and no storage reduce collection but do not make discussion anonymous. Distinctive explanations, volunteered personal details and visible dissent can identify a learner to classmates. Clearing cannot retract what others saw or copied. A correctable preview also cannot determine authorship, agreement or scientific capability. Design must make these limits actionable without adding identity checks or surveillance.

Proposed meaningful Design revision
Before: sequence 15 gives a general shared-screen limitation, editable dissent and temporary summaries; sequence 20 proposes conditional non-identifying inquiry notes.
After: place a short visibility notice beside entry fields, offer an explicit choice to discuss without entering text, and add a facilitator rule against treating browser wording as individual assessment evidence. Keep inquiry notes entirely outside the candidate. Any later collection proposal requires a separately reviewed purpose, minimum information, access arrangements, retention period and correction process. Removing names alone does not establish anonymity. This revision remains proposed until integrated; its benefits are unverified.

Candidate interface wording
Beside entries: “People nearby can see this screen. Use fictional plant evidence; do not enter names or personal details. You may discuss, draw or use paper without entering text.”
Beside preview: “Working wording for discussion. It does not verify who contributed, agreement or learning. Correct it or leave disagreement unresolved.”
Beside handoff: “Clear removes this activity's temporary writing and preview. It cannot remove copies or what others have seen. Refreshing or closing loses writing.”
Do not promise private dissent on the shared device. Do not add automatic personal-detail detection: it could miss disclosures or wrongly block legitimate explanation. Teachers should invite removal or replacement of unintended details without reading them aloud.

Delegation and accountable decisions
The candidate may display the invented A/B/C evidence, reveal C on request, preserve editable entries and assemble a literal preview. It must not evaluate reasoning, recommend grades, infer learner needs, certify agreement or decide who may proceed. Empty text means only text not supplied. No changed claim is required.
Teachers facilitate comparison, check whether recorder wording is acceptable to those represented, and permit retention, narrowing, revision or withholding. They can pause or switch routes when device control, reading burden or disagreement interferes with participation. Learners may decline browser recording without explaining why. The app cannot enforce these practices; they require review and facilitation.

Correction and exposure response
Make initial wording, current claim, support, uncertainty and dissent editable before and after preview. Regenerate the preview from current entries on request; remove obsolete preview copies on correction or confirmed clearing. Cancel preserves all writing. No undo crosses the handoff boundary.
If unintended personal information is entered, offer removal and paper continuation. Do not collect an incident account in the candidate. Any real disclosure response would follow the school's human process; this rehearsal supplies no approved process or authorization.

Non-AI alternative
Use prepared fictional A/B/C cards and the same comparison, uncertainty and reconsideration prompts in teacher-facilitated paper discussion. A learner can explain orally or draw without creating a written record. Paper is also visible and copyable; facilitators should avoid names and unnecessary retention. Paper-only delivery remains legitimate, with route equivalence unverified.

Rival explanations and unknowns
Sparse writing may reflect reading, vocabulary, typing, time, discussion pressure or comparison difficulty. Fluent wording may reflect copying, prior familiarity or recorder influence. Neither establishes capability. Unknowns include classroom visibility, languages, support staffing, discussion norms, device availability and preparation burden.

Review and next action
