Sequence 8 supplies fictional evidence; 13 and 15 specify correction, representation and recovery; 20 distinguishes supported practice from transfer; 22 specifies visibility and delegation limits. No participant observations, approval, measured outcomes or demonstrated proficiency exist.

Meaningful revisions adopted
Before: sequence 15 ends with a guided summary and general shared-screen limits. After: label the summary as supported discussion; add optional less-cued practice and a separate inquiry draft (20). Place visibility notices beside entries, explicitly permit discussion without browser recording and exclude inquiry notes from the candidate (22). These changes are reviewable design decisions, not verified benefits. No earlier artifact requires revision.

Layout and fictional cards
Use one responsive page: evidence first, editable reasoning next, preview last. Keep evidence accessible while editing. Use labelled native controls, keyboard operation, readable text, visible focus and information that does not depend on color. Accessibility remains unverified.
Every card says: “Invented classroom story: these numbers are story inputs, not study results.” Fictional period: 14 days. Water is arbitrary story units per day, not plant-care advice.
A: water 1; bright light; final height 12 cm; upright leaves.
B: water 2; dim light; final height 18 cm; drooping leaves.
C: water 2; bright light; final height 10 cm; upright leaves.
Always disclose: starting heights, plant type, soil and other conditions are unrecorded. Final height is not an increase; leaf descriptions do not establish health. “Better” needs a stated criterion.

Interaction specification
Initially show A/B. Offer claim choices “B is taller at the end,” “Taller means better,” “I cannot decide yet,” and original wording. Selecting a choice inserts editable wording only on request. Ask “What differs in observations and recorded conditions?” Provide an editable comparison entry; A/B differ in water and light.
A button reveals C, labelled additional evidence rather than a verdict. Allow return to A/B and reopening C without losing text. Invite A/C and B/C comparison. C challenges a generalization about more water always accompanying greater final height; it does not refute every claim or isolate causation.
Keep separately editable initial wording, current claim, comparison, supporting observations, uncertainty and optional dissent. Offer retain, narrow, revise or withhold without requiring a selection, text or changed claim. Initial wording is editable working text, not an authenticated first thought.
Preview assembles literal current entries and fixed missing-information text. Blank entries read “Text not supplied.” Include a user-selected representation description: one explanation, several explanations or representation unresolved; default to unresolved. Selection does not verify agreement. Editing invalidates the old preview; regenerate on request. No scores, completion badges, automated feedback or competence inference.

Visibility and recovery
Beside entries: “People nearby can see this screen. Use fictional evidence; do not enter names or personal details. You may discuss, draw or use paper without entering text.”
Beside preview: “Working wording for discussion. This does not verify contribution, agreement or learning. Correct it or leave disagreement unresolved.”
Clear for next group opens an explicit warning with Cancel and Clear. Cancel preserves all state. Confirmed clearing removes entries, selections and preview copies, resets C and announces the result; no undo crosses handoff. Explain that refresh or closing loses writing and clearing cannot retract copies or what others saw. Use temporary memory only: no network, external resources, identity fields, storage or participant notes.

Ready paper route and facilitator script
Copy the three cards above onto separate sheets; hold C until requested. Supply a response sheet: Initial wording; A/B differences; Additional pair compared; Current claim; Supporting observation; Uncertainty; Retain/narrow/revise/withhold; Alternative wording or dissent; Whose explanation is represented? All entries optional. Use the same visibility limits and correction invitation. Allow oral explanation, drawing, pointing with explanation or supported recording. Continue on paper after device failure without mandatory re-entry.
Ask “Which observation supports your wording?” and “What information would you need to call final height greater growth?” Make recorder wording available for correction. Roles are optional; passing preserves evidence access and later contribution. Do not use browser wording as individual assessment evidence.

Practice, inquiry and gates
Optional practice: “Choose another pair. What can you claim, and what remains uncertain?” Earlier prompts remain available. This is practice, not proof of independence. Separate paper inquiry draft: invented carts D—low ramp, smooth surface, distance 40 cm; E—high, rough, 55 cm; F—high, smooth, 35 cm. Numbers are story inputs; cart type, release method and repeated trials are unknown. Ask what supports, challenges or leaves unresolved “higher always means farther.” Similar patterns may invite copying. A delayed fresh task and any inquiry collection need separate human review.
Sparse writing may reflect reading, typing, time or pressure; fluent writing may reflect copying or recorder influence. Plant differences may involve water, light, starting height or other missing conditions. Field evidence remains pending. Hypothetical event
A learner writes: “B is taller at the end, but we do not know which grew more.” While exploring suggested claims on the shared device, the learner activates insertion of “Taller means better.” Suppose the candidate replaces the occupied claim field without preserving its previous wording. The learner objects that their uncertainty has disappeared. No implementation or interaction test has established that this occurs; the scenario exposes an unspecified replacement behavior.

Named assumption
Requesting insertion is sufficient evidence that a learner intends to replace existing wording and can recover any displaced qualification. This assumption first becomes actionable in the Design insertion specification, so Design is the earliest artifact requiring revision.

Requested requirement change
Before: sequence 24 says selecting a choice inserts editable wording only on request, without specifying occupied-field behavior.
After: show suggested wording without changing an entry. Direct insertion is allowed into an empty target. For an occupied target, identify the field and show the proposed replacement with explicit Replace and Cancel controls. Cancel preserves entries, selections, reveal state and any valid preview. Replacement preserves the immediately preceding target wording in temporary memory and offers “Restore previous wording” within the current group. Restoration requires a deliberate action and never occurs automatically. Replacement or restoration invalidates the discussion preview; regeneration remains user-triggered. Confirmed handoff clearing removes the recovery copy as well as all existing entries and preview copies. No restoration crosses handoff or survives refresh.

Human and non-AI route
A facilitator can invite correction without attributing the incident to learner ability. Use the same fictional evidence cards on paper; place optional suggested claims on a separate sheet so learners can inspect them while retaining their own wording. Oral explanation, drawing and paper-only delivery remain legitimate. Paper visibility and route equivalence remain unresolved.

Dissent, rivals and unknowns
A teacher might reject the added controls as excessive for a short discussion. Apparent loss of uncertainty could instead reflect intentional replacement, recorder influence or uncertainty that was spoken but never entered. The interface cannot determine intent, authorship or agreement. Unknowns include control comprehension, reading burden, shared-device discussion norms and the effort required to recover wording.

Implementation challenge and proposed Build change
Before: treating empty visible fields as sufficient evidence of complete handoff clearing.
After: define and inspect every application-owned copy: editable entries, preview nodes, pending proposal text, per-target recovery text and any temporary rendering references. Confirmed handoff must remove all of them. Recreate editable controls at handoff rather than relying only on assigning empty values, then investigate browser undo and autofill using fictional text. Do not describe this as secure erasure: browser-managed state, copies and what others saw remain outside that assurance. This makes sequence 29 concrete without requesting another Design revision.

Small candidate scope
Use one self-contained page with inline CSS and JavaScript and native labelled controls. Show fictional A/B initially and C on request: A—water 1, bright light, final height 12 cm, upright leaves; B—water 2, dim light, 18 cm, drooping leaves; C—water 2, bright light, 10 cm, upright leaves. Each card carries the invented-story label. State the fictional 14-day period, arbitrary water units and missing starting heights, plant type, soil and other conditions. Final height is not an increase; leaf wording does not establish health.
Maintain separate optional initial wording, current claim, comparison, support, uncertainty and dissent entries. Reconsideration and representation remain user descriptions, never judgments. Assemble requested output from literal entries using textContent, with blanks shown as “Text not supplied.” Include fixed limitations beside the output. No evaluation, compulsory revision or consequential score belongs in the candidate.

Transition contract
Use editing, replacement confirmation, restoration confirmation and clear confirmation states. While confirmation is pending, block other text-changing actions and freeze affected selections. Show the target, current wording and proposed wording; retain only the minimum pending copy. Cancel returns to editing without altering entries, selections, reveal state, recovery or a valid preview.
Insert a suggestion directly only into an empty target. Confirmed occupied-field replacement saves that target's immediately preceding wording. Further replacement updates only that target's recovery copy. Show the saved wording before deliberate restoration; confirm any displacement of subsequent edits. Restoration consumes its recovery copy. Editing, replacement, restoration and output-relevant selection changes remove the old preview; evidence reveal alone preserves it.
Confirmed clearing resets entries, selections, C visibility, preview, pending actions and all recovery copies. Announce clearing and provide no application undo across handoff. Opening or canceling clear must preserve state. Handle Escape as Cancel and return keyboard focus to the initiating control. These are proposed behaviors, not verified accessibility.

Review instrumentation without participant records
Use a manual reviewer worksheet outside the candidate with synthetic text, expected behavior, observed behavior and unresolved defects. Do not collect interaction counts, timestamps, task notes or learner traces in the browser.
Pending checks: replace occupied wording and Cancel; replace, edit again, then restore or Cancel; replace each target independently; edit after preview; hide/reopen C; cancel and confirm handoff; attempt restoration and browser undo after clearing; operate controls by keyboard. Inspect output with markup-like fictional text to ensure literal rendering. No checks have been run here. Passing technical checks would establish only those tested behaviors.

Prepared non-AI fallback
Copy the labelled A/B/C cards above onto separate sheets and hold C until requested. Provide optional matching response fields and separate suggested-claim slips. Learners may discuss, draw or use supported recording; expose recorder wording for correction. Continue on paper after failure without mandatory re-entry. Paper-only delivery remains legitimate; paper visibility and route equivalence are unresolved.

Before real use, require teacher, student and caregiver review plus human interaction testing. Examine reading burden, device access, discussion norms and teacher workload separately from scientific reasoning. Synthetic reviewer worksheet

Observed behavior and evidence location remain blank until execution. Classify outcomes as observed as expected, discrepancy or untested; these are technical descriptions, not learner scores.
Probe occupied insertion followed by Cancel; independent recovery for each target; restoration after further editing; preview invalidation; reveal/hide preservation; Escape and focus return; clear cancellation; confirmed clearing followed by attempted recovery and browser undo; literal markup-like text. Record application behavior separately from browser-managed history. No check has been run and no secure-erasure assurance follows.

Draft reasoning lenses for later human review
Seek an explanation connecting a claim to a specific observation; identifying recorded similarities and differences; distinguishing final height from increase; and explaining how missing conditions limit causal conclusions. Reconsideration may retain, narrow, revise or withhold with reasons. Treat each lens as evidenced in this task, ambiguous, not elicited or not observed, with a brief supporting example if a separately approved inquiry permits collection. No totals, grades, rankings or proficiency labels.
Accept speech, drawing, pointing with explanation, writing and supported recording. An empty browser field means text not supplied. A group explanation cannot establish individual capability. Correction, dissent and requests for support remain valid actions rather than failures.

Comparison proposal, not an authorized study
Use teacher-facilitated paper discussion as the complete non-AI comparison option. Match fictional evidence, available time, facilitator prompts and access supports as far as practicable; document differences rather than asserting route equivalence. Compare reasoning opportunities, correction, participation and teacher effort separately.
Self-selected routes cannot isolate a device effect. If a later reviewed inquiry compares routes within learners or groups, propose counterbalanced order and distinct matched fictional tasks; repeated A/B/C exposure risks practice effects. Any assignment method requires review. Report assistance, exposure, missing observations and implementation differences alongside findings. Neither synthetic checks nor a before/after discussion licenses a causal efficacy claim.

Transfer and retention
Sequence 20's cart task repeats the plant story's numerical pattern, so success could reflect pattern matching. Draft a fresh fictional task with a different evidence structure: for example, a challenged causal claim with no direct counterexample, requiring withholding because conditions differ. Review its language and scientific interpretation before use. Begin with an open prompt; retain evidence visibility and access supports, and distinguish explanatory hints from language assistance. A later task at a reviewed delay addresses retention separately. Immediate supported performance establishes neither retention nor transfer.

Prepare a synthetic coverage matrix crossing paper/shared-device routes, reading and language presentation, contribution modes and discussion arrangements. Mark each cell planned, checked or unknown; no cells are checked here. Later coverage must use only reviewed, voluntary information, never inferred disability or ability. No observed difference cannot establish equity when relevant coverage is absent.

Usable facilitation routine
Choose a target such as connecting a claim to an observation, comparing recorded conditions, or explaining a limitation. Ask the learner which comparison they want to discuss. Keep cards, language support and earlier prompts available.
Describe only what the learner actually offered. A conditional template is: “You compared __ and __ and pointed to __. Your explanation connects that observation to __. What remains uncertain?” If that connection was not offered, omit it. Do not praise response length or announce competence. Invite correction: “Does that describe what you meant?”
Offer one focused next question. For example, after an A/C comparison: “Which recorded conditions match, which differ, and what is unrecorded?” This prompt itself supplies a comparison structure; apply 67's claim-specific support rules if a separately reviewed inquiry records the episode. A facilitator who supplies a scientific inference must identify it as supplied rather than credit it as independently produced.
Invite optional retry using B/C, or permit the learner to revisit the same pair, retain a qualified claim, withhold judgment or stop. Ask what observation now supports the wording and why. Another pair within the plant activity is supported practice, not transfer. Repeating a supplied sentence does not establish understanding; explaining its application may provide supported task evidence if appropriately reviewed.

Practice card for rehearsal
Target reasoning action: __. Fictional comparison: __. Open invitation: __. Conditional feedback wording: __. Reasoning supplied by the prompt or feedback: __. Optional next attempt: __. Correction or dissent route: __. Unresolved access/workload question: __.

Fresh-task draft for later review
Use an entirely invented paper-bridge story: P has 1 layer, span 10 story units and reported load 3 story units; Q has 2 layers, span 15 and load 5; R has 3 layers, span 20 and load 7. All numbers are fictional inputs, not experimental results or construction guidance. Other conditions are unrecorded. Proposed claim: “Adding layers caused the larger reported load.” Open invitation: “What can these observations support, and what remains uncertain?”
Unlike the plant counterexample, the reported load increases throughout; every pair also changes span. The draft therefore invites scrutiny of causal attribution without a direct counterexample. It requires human review of wording, interpretation and access before use. It is a candidate task, not a validated transfer measure. Keep support available and describe supplied content relative to the exact relation examined. Performance would concern this task only.

A separate task after a reviewed delay would be needed to investigate retention; specify interval, intervening exposure and supports before any inquiry. No interval, task equivalence or retention result is established here.
